Below it: a chapter heading (CAPVT V.) with its title, then the paragraph opening with a large woodcut initial. No marginal notes. A gathering signature at the lower right of the text.

main_text.p: percipiat, tamen Euangelium hac sola fideli mente prehensum, sit potens Dei instrumentum ad totius credentis salutem: ita quoque de legitimo Sacramentorum usu statuamus oportet. Nam & externum ipsum verbum simplex signi appellatione comprehenditur, quum naturalia quoque ῥήματα[?], sicut recte inquit Philosophus, sint τὰ ἐν τῇ λαλουμένῃ[?] ψυχῇ[?] παθημάτων σημεῖα[?] : & Sacramentalia signa idcirco verbo simplici praedicato diuinitus adiiciantur, ut ad eundem finem & usum illi per fidei excitationem subserviant.
main_text.head: CAPVT V. De Sacramenti Cœna Domini, legitimè administratæ, fine & effectis.
main_text.p: Hoc etiam caput, ad quod dirigenda est tota superior disputatio, spiritus erroris miris modis depravauit, quò magis fidis omnibus seruis Dei enitedum est, ut de hac quoque doctrinæ parte liquido in Ecclesia Dei constet. Sumemus autem ad hoc explicandum argumentum, duos in primis Apostoli locos: unum, ex Roman. 4. ii. vbi duabus voculis, nempe Signi & Sigilli, propo-sito Circuncisionis exemplo, Apostolus tum quæ sit in genere forma-

page.notes: The Greek in the first paragraph is only partly legible on the scan; the marked words are uncertain. The Aristotle phrase (De Interpretatione) appears to be printed in an abbreviated or damaged form, and I have not been able to confirm each letter. The large initial "H" of "Hoc" is a woodcut letter. The ornament band between the paragraphs is decorative and not transcribed. The head "CAPVT V." and its title are read as one heading.
